correctness.rationale: The generic-fiber inequality and constant modulus are verified directly in the 2024 primary text. The resonant triple identity has equal sum and squares and is generic by 6h²!=0. Multiplicative ratio recurrence on odd prime-field lines gives p-th-root quadratic restrictions. The finite-difference identity (3) shows mixed third derivatives vanish for p>=5, so phase is Fp quadratic. SO2 invariance of its triple restriction and the complete eigenweight classification exclude exotic forms, forcing trace(c t²). Converse follows by Fourier translation. The packaged exact F_25 rank computation supports rather than replaces the uniform proof.

originality.rationale: The full 2024 primary work establishes the sharp constant and constant-modulus condition but does not classify the sixth-moment parabolic phases. Closest published records prove the prime-field n=1 family, which is a covered subcase, not a theorem about proper extension fields. This proof eliminates all non-field-linear prime-vector-space quadratic phases for every n and establishes exactly q^2 projective phases. Best-knowledge novelty only; unpublished/equivalent coverage remains a risk.

value.rationale: The original sharp constant and constant-modulus condition leave a natural phase-classification gap over nonprime fields. The answer controls every extension degree and shows why the many candidate quadratic prime-vector-space phases collapse to only q² field-trace characters. This has structural content relevant to sharp Fourier inequalities, rather than a numerical tweak or routine restatement.
